SOURCES & NOTES

Context matters.

PISA assesses how 15-year-old students apply knowledge. Scores are scale points, not percentages. Different subjects have distinct scales.

National averages conceal differences within countries. Score gaps do not explain causes and are not significance tests.

Coverage & geography

Science covers all 91 countries and economies in the OECD table. Computational problem-solving covers 85. Mathematics and reading each have 87 verified entries; Uzbekistan, Cyprus, Kenya and Rwanda remain unverified for these two subjects.

Grey land includes places with no entry for the selected subject. Regional results for B-S-J-Z (China), Ukrainian regions, Kurdistan Region (Iraq) and Dushanbe (Tajikistan) use representative dots, never whole-country shading.

* OECD flags sampling issues for some systems. Consult the source notes before comparison. Vietnam’s assessment-mode change prevents trend comparison. Map bands are descriptive, not proficiency levels. Boundaries do not imply a position on territorial status.
